target_customer: Consumers considering a tattoo, and local tattoo artists who receive bookings
problem: People fear regret from a permanent tattoo and cannot preview a design on their own body before booking.
business_model: Free AR app with in-app purchases, with a planned booking marketplace taking fees from tattoo artists
product_category: Augmented reality consumer app and marketplace

founders.name: Sasha Rohachova
founders.background_notes: Named Oleksandra Rohachova by TechCrunch. No background found.

founders.name: Pavlo Razumovskyi
founders.background_notes: Named CTO on the YC page and TechCrunch. No background found.

technical_complexity.rationale: Real time AR placement of designs on skin from a phone camera was achievable with 2016 mobile vision tools but needed solid computer vision work for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Several free tattoo try-on apps appeared, and users may prefer booking with artists they already know, per TechCrunch.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquirer found. The app continued under INKHUNTER, INC. and added AI design generation.

market_need_then: The app reached about 2.5 million iOS downloads by April 2016 per TechCrunch, showing strong consumer curiosity, but monetization beyond downloads was unproven.

branding.domain_note: Used inkhunter.tattoo as the listed website; a .com status was not found.
branding.community_and_virality: Covered by TechCrunch (2016), iMore and GearBrain reviews, and a Product Hunt launch with 353 upvotes on 2016-04-06.

brand_strength.rationale: Strong press and millions of downloads for a tiny team, with the app name itself describing the use, though no mascot or community beyond downloads was found.

pivots.to: B2B licensing of the AR technology as an SDK
pivots.why: TechCrunch reported the team looking toward a wider B2B play

pivots.to: Try and buy tattoo booking marketplace
pivots.why: TechCrunch reported the team shelved the SDK plan to drive bookings with local artists

outcome_analysis: INKHUNTER built a large free user base for a small team, then shifted from consumer app to B2B SDK to a booking marketplace. The YC directory marks the company inactive, yet the app remains listed under INKHUNTER, INC. with AI features, so the inactive label may reflect the company or the marketplace plan. No shutdown or post-mortem was found, so the cause is not public.
notes: The company site returned 503 so it was not read. The 120K figure is YC's standard deal as stated by TechCrunch and also appears in CB Insights (dated 2018-07-18). The 2016-06 seed with Entrepreneurs Roundtable Accelerator rests on CB Insights only; CB Insights total of 160K over 2 rounds implies roughly 40K unexplained for that round, and one listing names Mashup Ventures. A Medium post mentions New York investment without amounts. Product Hunt claims 8 million users, a self reported claim. The status conflict (YC inactive, app live) is unresolved. The only competitor sources found are undated alternativeto pages, so the list is empty.
